title: Avimi Nota’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Avodah Zarah 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.36b.2): “Bali said that Avimi Nota’ah said in Rav’s name: Their bread and their oil are among the eighteen matters.” [Shabbat 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.17b.4) reads “Bali said that Avimi Sanvata’ah said”; Hyman proposes the reading as in Avodah Zarah, which he also reports in Dikdukei Soferim. (Hyman takes it as a place-name, citing [Shabbat 121b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.121b.4), and the Arukh, entry נוות.)[^1]

notes.text: [Avodah Zarah](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.36b.2) gives Bali’s citation of Avimi of Nota in Rav’s name. [Shabbat 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.17b.4) has Avimi of Sanvata and gives the next chain to Rav Acha bar Adda. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.17b.4.1) calls Sanvata a place-name. The cited [Shabbat 121b passage](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.121b.4) mentions Ninveh. Rashi’s gloss does not identify a town. The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=151&lang=en) reports that the Arukh explains the name through Naioth in Ramah.
